view_observations.clay: Actual reticulate relief remains visible on the blade, especially the left half; faint but distinguishable from the parallel control at the same512px frame.
view_observations.silhouette: True black slab silhouette; not used to establish organ identity or Audit129. Matrix silhouette is intentionally shared with the control.

feature_criteria.evidence: Original KE1976 H.I.15 PlateIVe actual pixels and pp71-72, original inventory and frozen brief; entire isolated fossil blade only. Tip/base and net pattern are stylized, not a specimen scan or living whole organism.

Final top/reversehero/clay and actual GLB vein geometry show oblique side ridges plus inter-row bridges. Source supports repeated bifurcation/short bridges and preservation variation. No painted veins/textures.

Same decoded matrix and blade geometry, exact same generator, same ridge widths/heights and exact-equal comparison render config. Bjuvia control has transverse parallel veins with basal forks, not a blank leaf. Final candidate topology, not central rib, color, scale, pose, damage or labels, supplies distinction. feature_criteria.limits: The control is a deliberately normalized topology experiment, not a reconstruction of the incomplete Bjuvia specimen or approval of a separate Bjuvia asset. Bjuvia actual density12-14/cm is not reproduced at this illustrative physical scale (control primary spacing5.98mm); no numerical fossil-density/relief claim is accepted. Matching an unpreserved entire outline conservatively removes silhouette as a distinguishing cue; it does not assert that specimen preserved that outline.

defects.observation: Uniform grid-sized teeth at banks and very weak neutral geometry make the key fan/bar planform depend too strongly on color at512px. Actual channels do exist and connect; this is not a material-name-based claim of missing drainage.
defects.original_obligation: Original inventory: elongated bars/channels fanning from a river mouth and secondary texture subordinate to diagnostic geometry. Frozen brief: visibly downstream-widening mouths and unequal elongated bars separated by connected channels at256-512px.
defects.correction: Redistribute the current geometry budget from broad flat terrain to channel-aligned bank contours and long bar tips. Use continuous bank edges/controlled sloped cross sections to remove sample-grid teeth and make the principal mouths and bar boundaries legible in gray, retaining shallow original scale, connected side creeks and seaward widening. Do not conceal the defect with colors, depth bias, a different camera or arbitrary height exaggeration.
defects.retest: New revision with retained old evidence, exact GLB eight512px views plus same-scale neutral top; check primary banks in both obliques, actual water-network connectivity/widths, closed topology, visible overlaps, source re-export, two executed rebuilds, project/Khronos/Three checks. Targeted independent difference review only; do not repeat unaffected full-batch scientific research.

audit129_review.reason: The control is not accepted merely because its label says Bjuvia. Actual source photo/text support parallel transverse veins and a central rib, including possible basal forks. The controlled geometry contains these features; alternate key reveals them strongly, so it is not a blank control. Matching the entire unpreserved outline deliberately eliminates silhouette as a source of distinction; actual decoded matrix/leaf equality verifies this. Net side-relief, not central rib alone, remains the difference. This establishes the limited original qualitative neutral-material distinction, not quantified specimen reconstruction or a separate Bjuvia production approval.
audit129_review.limits: Control vein density is heavily simplified and not fossil-measured; physical12-14/cm not claimed. Source whole outline is incomplete; exact tip/base not reconstructed. At this specific512px evidence the net topology is visible but subtle. Approval does not extend to arbitrary smaller projections, view/light profiles or named-specimen fidelity.
